Phosphine-Catalyzed Annulations Based on [3+3] and [3+2]
Trapping of Ketene Intermediates with Thioamides
Yu-Hao Wang, † Zhen-Ni Zhao, † Subarna Jyoti Kalita, and Yi-Yong Huang *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 8147 −8152 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: With the aim of developing novel annulations via ketene intermediates, allenyl imide and alkynoates bearing good
leaving groups are used for their function in a tandem conjugate addition −elimination reaction (SN2 ′ type) promoted by
nucleophilic phosphine catalysts. By utilizing thioamides as 1 S,3N-bis-nucleophiles, [3+3] and [3+2] annulations have been
established to allow rapid access to 1,3-thiazin-4-ones and 5-alkenyl thiazolones in high yields, respectively. Furthermore, the
possible reaction mechanisms are proposed on the basis of deuterium labeling experiments and density functional theory
calculations.
E
ver since the groundbreaking report on elucidating the
structure of diphenylketene in 1905 by Staudinger, 1 the
generation and synthetic utility of ketenes have attracted a
great deal of interest from organic chemists.
2 As a class of
cumulenes, ketenes possess highly reactive carbonyl and
alkenyl groups, which makes them very useful chemical entities
and versatile reactive intermediates. As demonstrated in
industrial applications
3 and academic research, including
polymer science4 and organic synthesis such as total syntheses 5
and methodology development, 6 ketenes play a vital role. In
particular, they are e ﬀective in catalytic cycloaddition for
various types of carbo- and heterocycle synthesis. 7 Therefore,
the discovery of novel ketene intermediates and ketene-based
reactions represents a signi ﬁcant task.
By far, the most commonly used approaches for generating
ketenes are base-mediated elimination of HCl from acyl
chlorides
8 and Wol ﬀ rearrangement of diazo ketones. 9 In our
previous work, a phosphine catalyst promoted the generation
of reactive vinylphosphonium ketene species A through 1,4-
addition of PBu 3 and dissociation of a 2-oxazolidinyl anion
from allenyl imide, which was captured by various 1 C,1C-bis-
nucleophiles through [4+1] cycloaddition for the bis-electro-
philicity ( Scheme 1 a).10 On the basis of this work, we
envisaged that (1) thioamides 11 can be used as potential
1S,3N-bis-nucleophiles to capture vinylphosphonium-ketene
intermediate A to install N,S-containing heterocycles ( Scheme
1b) and (2) the employment of alkynoates containing a good
leaving group 12 may provide a [3]cumulene type of

phosphonium-ketene intermediate B through nucleophilic
phosphine catalysis, which may display unique reactivity in
the novel cycloaddition of thioamides ( Scheme 1 c). With the
purpose of advancing the synthetic potential of the
phosphonium-ketene intermediates and developing new types
of reactions, we perform these studies aiming at two types of
annulations with thioamides for building N- and S-containing
heterocycles, viz., 1,3-thiazin-4-one and 5-alkenyl thiazolones.
1,3-Thiazin-4-ones make up an important family of six-
membered heterocycles because of their bioactive activities.
13
For instance, in Figure S1 , BTZ043 can kill Mycobacterium
tuberculosis.14 The natural product Thiasporine A, isolated
from the marine-derived Actinomycetospora chlora SNC-032,
showed cytotoxicity against the non-small-cell lung cancer cell
line H2122.
15 Thus, the development of an e ﬃcient approach
to generating 1,3-thiazin-4-one core has attracted a great deal
of interest.16 Nucleophilic phosphine catalysis has emerged as a
powerful tool for the installation of various heterocycles,
relying on the interception of the reactive intermediate, via the
1,4-addition of phosphine to activated allene, by electrophiles
or nucleophiles.
17 To the best of our knowledge, there is no
precedent for using thioamides as bis-nucleophiles in the
allene-based cycloadditions.
18 Nevertheless, the formidable
challenge of controlling the chemo- and regioselectivities
resulting from the multiple reaction sites in the substrates will
be addressed.
To test the feasibility of installing a 1,3-thiazin-4-one
derivative from allenyl imide 1 and thiobenzamide 2a, PBu
3
was ﬁrst studied in dichloroethane at room temperature (rt)
(Table 1 , entry 1). 4 H-1,3-Thiazin-4-one 3a (49%) and 2 H-
pyrrol-2-one 3a′ (24%) generated through respective [3+3]
and [4+1] cycloadditions were isolated. The structure of 3a
was assigned by NMR and HRMS and further con ﬁrmed by X-
ray crystallography, 19 and thus, the hypothesis of using
thioamide as a 1 S,3N-bis-nucleophile to trap the proposed
vinylphosphonium ketene intermediate was validated. The use
of less nucleophilic phosphines, such as PhPMe
2,P h2PMe, and
PPh3, could increase the yield of product 3a gradually, whereas
a small amount of adduct 3a′ was still isolated (entries 2 −4).
To our delight, in the presence of a BnPPh 2 catalyst, the yield
of 3a reached 82% with marked suppression of the formation
of 3a′ (entry 5). When the reaction time was increased to 12 h,
the yield was further improved to 89% (entry 6). The
comparison without any catalysts indicated a messy reaction
mixture (entry 7). In addition, the screening of other solvents,
including CH
2Cl2, THF, toluene, benzene, and ethanol,
revealed that the protic solvent was preferred, because the
yield of 3a was dramatically increased to 99% in ethanol (entry
12).
With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, we focused
on the scope of various thioamides ( Scheme 2). Gratifyingly, a
range of 4 H-1,3-thiazin-4-one derivatives 3a−y were synthe-
sized in 32 −99% yields. First, the e ﬀect of substituents at the
para position of thioarylamides on the yield was studied. When
electron-donating groups were introduced, the Me group
provided a yield (92%) higher than that of the OMe group
(81%). Substrates having an active hydrogen group were
tolerated in the reaction, and the performance of the NH
2
group (95%) was much better than that of the OH group
(72%). Product 3f with a
tBu group was isolated in a yield
comparable to that of 3a. The use of substrates bearing
halogen substituents (F, Cl, and Br) provided the correspond-
ing products 3g−i, respectively, in 84 −97% yields. Thereafter,
the substrates with electron-withdrawing groups (CF
3,N O 2,
and CN) were applied to a ﬀord <60% yields ( 3j−l), which
resulted from the undesired aza-Michael addition of thioamide
to allene. Next, diverse substituents at the meta position of

thioarylamides were investigated. Compared with the same
group at the para position, the OMe and CF 3 groups delivered
superior outcome ( 3m, 93%; 3p, 55%), albeit we produced
much lower yields for the Cl and Br groups ( 3n, 75%; 3o,
66%). When using ortho-substituted substrates (Cl and Br),
moderate yields were obtained ( 3q, 66%; 3r, 58%). The
employment of meta,para-disubstituted thioarylamides indi-
cated that Me groups ( 3s, 92%) were more suitable than Cl
groups (3t, 72%). The synthesis of the 2-naphthyl derivative of
4H-1,3-thiazin-4-one (3u) was achieved in 94% yield. Likewise,
heterocyclic substrates bearing 2-furyl and 2-thienyl groups
underwent [3+3] cycloaddition to give products 3v and 3w in
71% and 67% yields, respectively. In addition, 4 H-1,3-thiazin-
4-ones 3x and 3y from thiourea and thiopivalamide were
aﬀorded in 67% and 83% yields, respectively.
Using the tandem 1,4-addition of phosphine and elimination
of a leaving group (SN2 ′ type reaction) described above to
generate ketene intermediates, we continued to pursue new
candidates to check the reactivity with thioamides. 3-
Arylpropiolates bearing 4-nitrophenyl as a good leaving
group can act as Michael acceptors and have been successfully
utilized in annulations involving alkyne acyl ammonium and
azolium intermediates through nucleophilic amine and N-
heterocyclic carbene (NHC) catalysis.
20 Herein, 4-nitrophenyl
3-arylpropiolates were studied for the ﬁrst time in nucleophilic
phosphine-catalyzed annulations, and the key intermediate
involved was quite unlike those in amine and NHC catalysis
for the 1,4-addition model instead of the 1,2-addition model of
the catalyst to arylpropiolate. The optimization results using
thiobenzamide 2a and 4-nitrophenyl 3-phenylpropiolate 4a
were shown in Table S1 . Eventually, [3+2] cycloaddition
through C(O) −N and α-S−C bond formation occurred,
delivering 5-alkenyl thiazolone 5a in ≤81% yield in the
presence of 30 mol % PBu
3 and Cs 2CO3 (1.2 equiv) ( Scheme
3). Herein, the role of Cs 2CO3 is to neutralize the 4-
nitrophenol byproduct (pKa ∼ 7.22), which is more acidic than
that of the 2-oxazolidinone byproduct mentioned above (p Ka
∼ 12.78). It should be noted that 5-alkenyl thiazolones have
been recognized as important moieties in many bioactive
molecules ( Figure S1 )
21 and as substrates for synthetic
methodology development. 22 Typically, 5-alkenyl thiazolones
are synthesized by Knoevenagel condensation of thiazolin-4-
ones and aldehydes.
23 It should be mentioned that 4 Å
molecular sieves (MS) were detrimental to the yield.
The substituent aryl groups for two substrates were validated
under the optimized reaction conditions, and the results are
summarized in Scheme 3.B y ﬁxing the use of alkynoate 4a,w e
investigated the scope of various aromatic, heteroaromatic, and
aliphatic thioamides ( ≤92% yield). Thioarylamides with a Me
group at the para position provided yields comparable to or
slightly higher than those of halogen groups (54 −68%), while
much higher yields were obtained when incorporating OMe
and
tBu groups ( 5c, 92%; 5d, 87%). The electron-withdrawing
group (CF3) at the same position resulted in a lower yield ( 5h,
46%). The same tendency of the substituent e ﬀect was also
observed at the meta position, and a better result was achieved
for the electron-donating group ( 5i, OMe, 73%; 5j,C F3, 49%).
When a Cl group was introduced at the ortho position,
cycloadduct 5k was formed in 71% yield. Notably, the
performance of the substrate with a 2-furyl group was very
superior to that of the 2-thienyl case ( 5l, 92%; 5m, 61%).
Moreover, 2-naphthyl-substituted thioamide was examined to
produce 5n in 79% yield. tert-Butyl thioamide was also
tolerated, and the corresponding product 5o was a ﬀorded in
57% yield. Next, other ﬁve 3-arylpropiolates underwent the
[3+2] cycloaddition of thiobenzamide 2a to give the
corresponding 5-alkenyl thiazolones 5p−t in 70 −80% yields.
5-Alkenyl thiazolones feature the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl
scaﬀold. To demonstrate the synthetic versatility of 5-alkenyl
thiazolones empowered by nucleophilic phosphine catalysis,
two sets of one-pot sequential reactions were examined. Under
the standard reaction conditions mentioned above, thiazolone
5a was ﬁrst generated, which then underwent Me
2PPh-
catalyzed [4+2] annulation of α-Bn-substituted allenoate 6
for 6,7-dihydro-5 H-pyrano[2,3-d]thiazole 7 (Scheme 4 a),24
and PBu3-catalyzed formal β-acylation with acyl chloride for 5-
arylidene thiazolone 8 (Scheme 4 b).25
The proposed reaction mechanism for the syntheses of 1,3-
thiazin-4-one 3 begins with formation of vinylphosphonium
ketene intermediate I from 1 and BnPPh 2 (Scheme 5 ). The
amide nitrogen anion, generated via the deprotonation of 2 by
the oxazolidinyl anion, adds preferentially to the sp-hybridized

generate nitrogen anion III, which undergoes 6- endo-trig
cyclization by way of sulfur anion resonance form III′ followed
by the elimination of BnPPh
2 to give 1,3-thiazin-4-one 3.T o

Compared with the [3+3] cycloaddition of allenyl imide and
thioamide, the proposed reaction mechanism of [3+2]
cycloaddition using alkynoate also comprises a tandem
phospha-Michael addition/elimination/nucleophilic addition
of ketene intermediate by the N anion sequence at the
beginning ( Scheme 6 ), forming similar types of intermediates
with di ﬀerent substituents in the C C bond region ( III and
IX). Thereafter, two distinct models of cyclization were
observed. For the former case, V could likely be formed but
without a good termination pathway, and it would go
backward to III. On the contrary, starting from alkynoate
and thioamide, the intramolecular addition
26 (5-exo-trig
cyclization) of intermediate IX to provide [3+2] cycloadduct
4a is preferred rather than 6- endo-trig cyclization probably due
to the more steric hindrance at the β-position of intermediate
IX than that at the α-position.
Furthermore, the transformation from intermediate X to XI
involving 1,2-H transfer was understood through density
functional theory (DFT) calculations by using the Gaussian 16
suite of programs (see the details in the Supporting
Information). Four possible approaches were considered (see
Figure S2 ). Direct 1,2-H transfer without any assistance was
ﬁrst excluded because of a high energy barrier ( ΔG
⧧ = 38.8
kcal/mol). H 2O-assisted 1,2-H transfer in a stepwise manner
appears to be more favorable, which exhibits activation
energies ( ΔG⧧ = 18.0 and 8.4 kcal/mol) much lower than
that of the synchronized manner ( ΔG⧧ = 28.1 kcal/mol); it is
consistent with the inferior result upon using 4 Å MS to
remove a trace amount of water (see the result in entry 12 of
Table S1 ).
27 By comparison, the 1,2-H transfer between two
molecules of intermediate X was also studied, which seems less
possible on the basis of the Gibbs free energy change pro ﬁles
(see the details in the Supporting Information ).
In summary, we have demonstrated the novel phosphine-
catalyzed [3+3] and [3+2] annulations of allenyl imide and
alkynoates with thioamides involving vinylphosphonium and
[3]cumulene types of phosphonium ketene intermediates,
respectively, providing new entries to 1,3-thiazin-4-ones (25
examples, ≤99% yield) and 5-alkenyl thiazolones (20
examples, ≤92% yield) under mild conditions. The key proton
transfer steps were understood on the basis of deuterium
labeling experiments and DFT calculations. The synthetic
utilities of 5-alkenyl thiazolone were shown through two sets of
sequential phosphine-catalyzed derivatizations in one pot. The
methods reported here harness the power of ketene
intermediates and will open up the opportunity to enrich the
nucleophilic phosphine catalysis strategies for creating new
types of heterocycles.
